claim: The original Lu, Song, Zhang finding that language shifts LLM style is unverified here (page blocked) and is disputed by a preprint the journal declined.

Model origin does not predict cultural style as expected: US model drew more objects and more relational pairings than the Chinese model (d=1.38 on relational-minus-categorical score), opposite to the human East-Asian pattern.
LLM expressed values move far more under irrelevant context (mean shift up to |d|=5.86) than human values move over years or primes (largest d=0.53); an LLM is not one stable individual.

Default LLM answers resemble US and Western European respondents; prompting a country helps on average (cuts mean distance e.g. 2.42 to 1.57 for GPT-4o) but worsens roughly 20-29% of countries and relies on stereotype.
Country-level alignment of LLMs with Hofstede scores is weak and unstable (only one significant country-value correlation in Kharchenko et al.; Cao et al. correlations rest on 5 countries).
Persona prompts using real respondents align better for high-class, educated personas and the US than Egypt; marginalised individuals are modelled worse.

Group labels explain little of individual variation in LLM simulation: demographics explain <10% of annotation variance, while a two-hour personal interview lifts GSS normalized accuracy to 0.83 vs 0.74 for demographics (confirmed in paper).
LLMs prompted with identity labels misportray groups (out-group view) and flatten variance relative to real members.
Persona prompting gives high-arousal/low-arousal affect images matching stereotype but text answers do not; authors blame RLHF flattening (untested).
Caption holistic share in VLMs depends on the judge, language and image content (e.g. 26.10% on COCO to 73.37% on Japanese photos for GPT-4o-JP 6-shot); human judges disagree with GPT-4o on size.
Most citing papers (60 checked as snippets) repeat Na et al. without a direct replication; the construct is treated as reliable for group but not individual differences.
Culture in LLM work is usually proxied by country or language (37 of 90 region, 35 of 90 language), not defined.
Na et al. 2010 full text read: one US sample N=235, mean r=.008 (45 social pairs) and .038 (cognitive), first factors 12.26% and 10.69%; five-culture check of two tasks: person r=.04, culture r=.73.
